chunks.text: District-wise rainfall distribution of States is attached in Annexure I. 3. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 7th August 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 135.28 billion cubic meter, which is 74.1% of total live storage capacity (182.496 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 107 percent of last year's storage and 124 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. | 2 b) Groundwater Levels: About 43.1% of the total monitoring wells show depth to water level in the range of 0 to 5 m below ground level and 37.6% show depth to water level in the range of 5 to 10 m below ground level. About 19.2% of the total monitoring wells show water level deeper than 10 m below ground level. The groundwater level fluctuation analysis of Pre-monsoon 2025 with decadal mean of Pre-monsoon (2015-2024) indicates that 67.7% of analysed wells are showing rise and 33.0% are showing fall in water level. Remaining 0.3% stations analysed do not show any change in water level.

chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text:
As per the Ground Water Drought Indices (GWDI), in pre-monsoon 2025, 90% of the analysed wells are in the normal category, while 10% of the analysed wells are in the drought category. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Kharif 2025, certified seed availability is 178.64 lakh quintals against a requirement of 164.05 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 14.60 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 4. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Rice (Varieties: PR 114, PR 126 & PR 131) (Southern Rice Black Streaked Dwarf Virus (SRBSDV)) in Haryana and (Swarming Caterpillar) in Assam. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 5. chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
- During the week (07 Aug - 13 Aug 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 25%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01 June to 13 Aug 2025) shows no departure from LPA. Rainfall Forecast: - The monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Bhuj, Ahmedabad, Akola, Ramgundam, center of well marked Low pressure area over west central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal & north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts. - Rainfall is likely to be above normal over most part of Central India, West India, Odisha, Jharkhand, and many parts of NW India, Telangana, and Gangetic West Bengal. Below Normal over south Uttar Pradesh and many parts of NE India, Kerala, Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra Pradesh.

chunks.heading: 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION
chunks.text:
Soil Moisture Observation - Soil moisture as on 14 August 2025 was similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of M.P, central parts of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Haryana, Punjab, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, Rayalseema region of A.P., Tamil Nadu and southern parts of Bihar. - It was lower than average of past 9 years in Northern parts of Bihar, in parts of Assam, north eastern parts of U.P., Assam, Gujarat, in western and southern parts of Rajasthan, southern parts of Odisha, few western districts of MP and coastal districts of AP. | 7


Kharif Crops - Area coverage - Rice: About 398.59 lakh ha (98.9% of Normal) area coverage under Kharif Rice as compared to 362.92 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Moong: About 33.70 lakh ha (94.4% of Normal) area coverage under Moong as compared to 32.76 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Soybean: About 119.82 lakh ha (94.2% of Normal) area coverage under Soybean has been reported as compared to 124.59 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Sugarcane: About 57.31 lakh ha area coverage under Sugarcane has been reported as compared to 55.68 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

chunks.heading: 7. PEST & DISEASE
chunks.text:
- Farmers were informed to maintain good sanitation in the field and to avoid waterlogging conditions and unnecessary spray of insecticides if vectors are not present in the field. - They were also advised
| 10 to install light traps to monitor WBPH population and where less than 5 % incidence was observed, farmers were advised to spray neem oil as per label claim. - Print media advisories were published/circulated to create awareness among farmers. - Diseased Samples were taken from various rice growing districts and ICAR- NRIIPM will confirm and provide the report after identification/confirmat ion in lab Rice Assa m Nalbari, Baksa, Lakhimpur, Chirang, Jorhat, Biswanath Survey / NPSS Swarming Caterpilla r 6335.24 - Pest incidence was reported on 30.07.2025 & 07.08.2025 - Advisory issued through State WhatsApp group. - Regular monitoring is being carried out by all field functionaries as follow up action. - Officials from District Agriculture office are creating awareness programme among the farmers. - Total 2669.24 ha area treated/ controlled till date. | 11
